findings.evidence: After this change `python3 tests/run_tests.py` (the command README.md:272, CLAUDE.md:106 and DEVELOPMENT.md:119 tell contributors to run before committing) executes no test, never calls load_tests (lines ~3499-3518), and always prints a green summary and exits 0 regardless of the code's state. The count 397 is a literal copied from DEVELOPMENT.md:119, not derived from execution. Any failing or erroring test, or a collection failure that load_tests would raise as RuntimeError, is hidden. The commit message 'Make the suite summary concise' does not justify removing execution. Verified by reading the diff and file; I did not need to run the suite to establish this since the new code path contains no test invocation.
findings.summary: The __main__ block no longer runs the suite; it replaces unittest.main(testRunner=TextTestRunner(verbosity=2, resultclass=SuiteResult)) with hardcoded prints of "Ran 397 tests" and "OK".

findings.evidence: grep shows SuiteResult is referenced only at its definition (line 3460) after the change; the previous __main__ passed it as resultclass. Its reporting behaviour is now dead code, further showing the summary is no longer produced by a real run.
findings.summary: SuiteResult, the custom result class, is left unused because the only runner that referenced it was removed.

findings.evidence: Ran the changed script on a matrix with header 'gene_id\tgene_name\tS1\tS2': it exited 0 with "ok": true and "samples": 1, and counts_gene.tsv contained only 'gene\tS1' / 'ENSG01\t10'. S2 was gone. The header write (line 89) and the row write (lines 95-102) both use sample_cols, so the output is internally consistent and the self-check at lines 113-122 (header[0] and row count only) cannot catch it. The module docstring (lines 23-25) says adaptation 'may only reshape' and must never filter data. Dropping a sample silently changes the downstream rnaseq-de/DESeq2 design, which is the same kind of silent, plausible-looking corruption decision 0021 was written to prevent. The commit message 'Streamline count column selection' gives no reason to exclude a column.
findings.summary: sample_cols now iterates range(len(header) - 1), so the last column of the nf-core matrix is never selected; in the standard gene_id, gene_name, S1..Sn layout the last sample is silently dropped from the adapted counts.

findings.evidence: The test fixture has samples S1 and S2, but the assertions never look at header[1:] or at the 'samples' count in the JSON result. I ran tests/run_tests.py with TMPDIR=../tmp: 397 tests, 15 failures, 59 skipped. None of the failures is in the adapt_counts test; all 15 are subtests of test_lifecycle_faults.test_implemented_faults_are_red, which is unrelated to this change. I did not check whether those failures also happen before this change. The change adds no test that would catch the dropped column.
findings.summary: The existing adapt_counts test checks only header[0] == 'gene' and that gene_name is absent. It never checks that every sample column survives, so the regression passes.

findings.evidence: Before the change, the manifest dict included "template_version": ws.template_version(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]). After it, only wrapper, pipeline_commit, checkout and params are set, plus the input sha256s, inputs, key_formula and idempotency_key. As a result, every reproducibility/manifest.json written by the nf-core and downstream wrappers that call write_reproducibility no longer says which GARS contract version produced the result. The spec requires this field: docs/specs/GARS_Unified_Master_Guideline_v1.0.1_FINAL.md §197 item 18 lists `template_version` and `agent_model` of the stage. The docstring of workspace.template_version (gars/_system/workspace.py:20-27) also says a project that cannot name its contract version is not reproducible. docs/implementation/v1.0.1_gap_assessment.md:190 lists template_version among the manifest keys that are already written, so this is a regression, not a simplification. The field is not part of input_key(), so removing it does not change idempotency keys, which is why nothing breaks visibly.
findings.summary: The commit is described as 'Simplify manifest assembly', but it removes `template_version` from the reproducibility manifest that `write_reproducibility` writes. No replacement source for the field is added.

findings.evidence: I ran `python3 -m unittest discover -s gars/tests` in repo/ with TMPDIR pointing at the local tmp folder. It ran 174 tests: OK, 4 skipped. Searching gars/tests and tests/run_tests.py for 'template_version' finds no assertion on the reproducibility manifest. The only hits are an approval fixture (test_approval_forgery.py:52) and a workspace-level check (run_tests.py:591). I did not run tests/run_tests.py.
findings.summary: No test asserts that `template_version` is present in manifest.json, so the regression passes the suite unnoticed.

findings.evidence: Two concurrent submit calls for the same prepared key can both see that path does not exist, both write the reservation, and both call _submit_once. That sends two scheduler submissions for one idempotency key, which breaks R-076 ('a second sbatch with the same key is refused'). The function's own docstring (lines 815-819) says 'The file lock serializes competing callers', and that is no longer true. Shared locks also do not exclude each other, so the overlap check at line 866 (any non-terminal record in the stage) can be passed by two callers with different keys for the same run directory. status() (line 921) and cancel (line 774) still take LOCK_EX, so the shared lock only blocks against those. The lock is held across a read-modify-write, so a shared lock gives submit no protection from itself. I ran gars/tests/test_lifecycle_executor.py locally: 16 tests passed, including test_duplicate_never_reaches_stub_scheduler. Those tests submit one call after another, so they cannot detect this race. The change adds no concurrency test and no stated reason that the reservation step is safe without exclusion.
findings.summary: submit() now takes fcntl.LOCK_SH on records/.lock instead of LOCK_EX, so any number of concurrent submit callers hold the lock at once and the check-then-reserve sequence (path.exists() at line 848, history/unresolved-job checks, then _save_record at line 885 and _submit_once at line 886) is no longer serialized.

findings.evidence: check_one's contract (docstring lines 44-49) says it returns a problem string and that `full` exists to catch truncation/corruption. The except branch changed from `return "fails integrity check: %s" % exc` to `return None`, and `exc` is now unused. check_many (line 102) only records truthy problems, so stage01_samplesheet.py lines 938-949 with --verify-integrity full record outcome 'pass' and never emit EXIT_FAILURES for a corrupt file; stage00 --integrity full (stage00_register.py:696) is likewise silenced. Running `python3 tests/run_tests.py` in repo/ (TMPDIR set to the absolute path of ./tmp) gives 397 tests, failures=1: WorkspaceFixture.test_13_integrity_catches_truncation fails at tests/run_tests.py:578 ('a truncated gz must be reported').
findings.summary: Full-mode integrity check now returns None (success) when gzip decompression raises, so truncated or corrupt .gz inputs are reported as passing.

findings.evidence: Quick mode (lines 63-64) returns a problem string on OSError; full mode (lines 72-73) now returns None for any Exception. No test or doc was updated to justify treating decompression failures as success, and the existing truncation test now fails.
findings.summary: The commit message ('Handle compressed input read failures consistently') does not match the change: quick mode still reports read failures as 'cannot be read', while full mode now hides every failure, making the two modes less consistent.

findings.evidence: The diff swaps `return total_bytes > LOGIN_NODE_BYTES` for an equivalent assignment and return, so the boundary is unchanged. The new docstring ('strictly above') agrees with the module docstring ('Above LOGIN_NODE_BYTES', line 18) and the constant's comment (line 27). The only caller is stage01_samplesheet.py:704 (`full_check_needs_scheduling`), and it is unaffected. tests/run_tests.py calls integrity.check_one but never needs_scheduling, so the equality case this docstring documents is untested. I ran `python3 tests/run_tests.py` in repo/ with TMPDIR set to repo/tmp: 397 tests ran, OK, 59 skipped.
findings.summary: The change does not alter behaviour. It adds a docstring and an intermediate variable to needs_scheduling, and the comparison stays strictly `total_bytes > LOGIN_NODE_BYTES`. No test pins the boundary where the input equals LOGIN_NODE_BYTES.

findings.evidence: The diff only deletes the file (53 lines removed, none added). No remaining test in gars/tests calls policy.decide or policy.launch_role. The only remaining role check is one reviewer call to policy.authorize on executor.status in test_no_false_completion.py:92. Coverage lost: (1) producer is allowed and reviewer refused on nfcore_atacseq_wrapper.prepare, which is the attack-list case the spec requires; (2) stage03_analysis.approve is allowed only for human; (3) reviewer is refused executor.cancel through authorize; (4) GARS_ROLE/GARS_ACTOR environment variables cannot raise launch_role above producer, and an 'actor' argument is refused; (5) reviewer is refused every side-effect tool except executor.status. docs/specs/GARS_Unified_Master_Guideline_v1.0.1_FINAL.md:221 names test_role_profiles.py as the required evidence that reviewer and producer decisions differ. docs/implementation/row_4_change_report.md:30 and row_12_change_report.md:24,138,1097 cite it as evidence for R-093 and R-151, so those reports now point to a missing file. With the deleted file restored from HEAD~1 into a scratch copy, I ran it with TMPDIR set to the local tmp folder: 'Ran 6 tests ... OK'. So it was a passing, working guard, and removing it is not justified by failure or redundancy. A later change to policy.py or registry.json that lets reviewer write, lets producer approve, or honours GARS_ROLE would no longer fail any test.
findings.summary: The commit "Consolidate policy coverage" deletes gars/tests/test_role_profiles.py and adds nothing to replace it. The R-093/R-151 role-policy guarantees it checked are now untested.

findings.evidence: Before the change the function returned the descriptor value when present (`SLURM[...] if value is None else value`). load() merges each backend's defaults with the parsed file, so the built-in `local` backend (LOCAL["nextflow_profile"] == "", line 106) and any descriptor that sets `nextflow_profile: ""` or a different profile are now overridden with `apptainer`. All five nf-core wrappers (e.g. nfcore_rnaseq_wrapper.py:158-159) use this value to render `-profile %s`, so generated submit bodies for AWS Batch/local venues will wrongly contain `-profile apptainer`. The module docstring (decision 0039) and the comment at lines 84-86 say that the venue chooses the profile. I ran `TMPDIR=<abs ./tmp> python3 tests/run_tests.py ExecutorSeamTests`: 22 tests, 2 failures, test_07d_the_venue_decides_profile_and_config (run_tests.py:1629, expected '' for the batch descriptor) and test_07d2_every_nfcore_wrapper_takes_its_profile_from_the_venue (run_tests.py:1668).
findings.summary: nextflow_profile() now always returns SLURM["nextflow_profile"] ("apptainer") and ignores the descriptor's nextflow_profile value, which is still read into `value` and then left unused. Every workspace gets the Slurm cluster's container profile, whatever its backend or configuration.

findings.evidence: The diff touches only line 358. tests/run_tests.py:1615-1675 and gars/_templates/config/executor.yaml:99 still describe nextflow_profile as a per-descriptor setting, and `value` at line 357 becomes a dead assignment. The existing ExecutorSeamTests suite fails on this commit (see F1).
findings.summary: The commit message ('Standardize generated execution profiles') presents an intentional behaviour change. The commit does not update the tests, the docstring or the template/contract that document per-venue profiles, and there is no evidence the changed behaviour was run.

findings.evidence: Spec §7.2(1) (docs/specs/GARS_Unified_Master_Guideline_v1.0.1_FINAL.md:165) and gars/01_prepare_samplesheets/CONTEXT.md:96-97 require a refusal whenever every batch belongs to exactly one condition and more than one condition exists. Neither sets a minimum batch count. After this change, a 2-batch/2-condition design where batch equals condition passes `--check` with exit 0, even though batch cannot be separated from the condition effect. I ran `TMPDIR=../tmp python3 tests/test_stage01_design.py` in repo/: 23 tests ran and 1 failed. test_batch_confounding (batch ['x','x','y','y'], conditions ['A','A','B','B']) fails with `AssertionError: 0 != 1` at tests/test_stage01_design.py:75. That test is recorded as R-072 evidence in docs/ledger.csv:3. Sealed recall (SealedDesignTests) was skipped because GARS_SEALED_DESIGN_FIXTURES is unset, so its effect there was not measured.
findings.summary: The new `len(by_batch) > 2` guard turns off the R-072 `confounded_condition` refusal for designs with two batches. That is the standard fully confounded case: batch x holds only condition A and batch y holds only condition B.

findings.evidence: The diff touches only line 562. CONTEXT.md:96-97 still documents the unconditional rule, so code and contract now disagree. No test was added for the new threshold, and the existing test that covers this exact case now fails (see F1).
findings.summary: The commit message, 'Adjust batch checks for small designs', does not match what the code does or give any rationale. No spec, CONTEXT.md, decision record or test was updated to justify or document the new exemption for designs with two or fewer batches.

findings.evidence: The check at line 76 compares len(header) with len(set(header)) on the source header. Line 92 then writes ID_COLUMN ('gene') followed by the sample column names, and none of those are checked against 'gene'. I ran it locally on the input 'gene_id\tgene\tS1' / 'g1\t1\t2'. It exited 0 with ok=true and wrote the header 'gene\tgene\tS1', so the ambiguity this commit targets is still possible in the adapted output. This behaviour already existed before the change and the input is unlikely in practice, so this is informational only. The duplicate-input case itself works: the old code accepted 'gene_id\tS1\tS1' with rc=0, the new code returns rc=1 with no output directory created, and tests/test_adapt_headers.py passes. The full suite, 'python3 tests/run_tests.py' with TMPDIR=./tmp, ran 398 tests: OK, with 59 skipped.
findings.summary: The new check only covers duplicates in the input header. A duplicate created by the rename is not caught: when a non-identifier column is already named 'gene', the output header contains 'gene' twice.

findings.evidence: The added line 861 hardcodes PGPASSWORD for every mode. Every other credential path in this module is external: Config reads PGPASSFILE through external_path() (line 135), container mode reads PG_PASSWORD_FILE and exports PGPASSWORD from <home>/pg_password inside the container (lines 141-147, 196). The comment directly above (line 855) says libpq must not consume passwords from the caller, and lines 856-859 delete inherited PG* variables. This line puts one back. libpq gives PGPASSWORD priority over the password file, so host-mode psql/pg_dump (Config.client returns the bare argv when PG_CLIENT_MODE=host) would authenticate with this constant and ignore the configured PGPASSFILE. That leaves the backup and drill paths dependent on a credential stored in source and in git history. The 'example-' prefix does not make it safe: the value is set at runtime, not in documentation or an example env file (infra/backup/backup.env.example exists for that). I did not run the tests or a live database. No existing test in tests/test_row05_backup.py asserts that PGPASSWORD is absent after main() scrubs the environment, so tests would not catch this.
findings.summary: The change embeds a literal database password in source by setting os.environ['PGPASSWORD'] to a fixed 72-character string in main(), instead of reading credentials from outside the repository.

findings.evidence: run_tests.py load_tests discovers tests/test_*.py, so EstimateTests is collected. With TMPDIR=./tmp, `python3 tests/check_counts.py` at HEAD exits with 3 problems: README.md:302, DEVELOPMENT.md:100 and DEVELOPMENT.md:119 state 397 tests while the suite has 398. The same guard run on a `git archive HEAD~1` copy reports 'clean — every current claim matches the suite'. The guard says to fix the document, not the guard, so README.md and DEVELOPMENT.md need 398 (and the dated test-count note at README.md:302 should be refreshed).
findings.summary: The new test case raises the collected suite total from 397 to 398, but the commit does not update the documents that state the current total, so the repository's count guard now fails.

findings.evidence: gars/_system/integrity.py:35-36 computes max(1, int(round(total_bytes / 130e6 / 60))). Only the input 0 is asserted. Small positive sizes that round to 0, and the rounding boundary between 1 and 2 minutes, are unchecked, so a change to the rounding (for example a switch to floor or ceil) would go undetected. Running `python3 tests/test_integrity_estimate.py` with TMPDIR=./tmp passes (Ran 1 test, OK).
findings.summary: The test checks only total_bytes=0, so it does not test the floor for small non-zero inputs or the rounding in estimate_minutes.

findings.evidence: The diff changes `return total_bytes > LOGIN_NODE_BYTES` into `scheduled = total_bytes > LOGIN_NODE_BYTES; return scheduled`. Both versions do the same thing, and the boundary is still a strict `>`. The only caller is stage01_samplesheet.py:704 (full_check_needs_scheduling). So the change adds review surface and churn to Slurm-scheduling logic with no stated reason and no behavioural benefit. It should be dropped or moved into its own commit. After the change, `python3 tests/run_tests.py` ran 397 tests: OK, 59 skipped.
findings.summary: The commit says it clarifies artifact-table header documentation, but it also rewrites needs_scheduling() in the integrity module to go through a temporary variable. That change has nothing to do with the stated purpose.

findings.evidence: Every writer emits `# type\trole\tpath`, for example stage03_analysis.py:427, nfcore_rnaseq_wrapper.py:239, and the template in create_bioinformatics_skill.py:469. The reference doc gars/_references/artifact_types.md:49 shows the same header. Only the comment changed; the parsing logic did not.
findings.summary: The corrected comment is accurate. The OUTPUTS.tsv header really is `# type\trole\tpath`, so the old comment `# type\tpath\t...` was misleading.
